# R0 Digest — Author's Preface (lines 187–219)
**Source:** Tsumura, *The Second Book of Samuel* (NICOT, 2019)
**Reader:** main-thread
**Coverage:** lines 187–219 read in full

## Claims

### C-R0-01 | Concluding volume; Harrison commission for philology
- **Claim (attributed Tsumura):** This is the second and concluding volume on 1–2 Samuel. R. K. Harrison invited Tsumura (Semitic philologist, non-native English speaker) to deal with the difficult Hebrew text philologically; agreed to let the stories themselves give theological/devotional insights rather than imposing them.
- **Quote:** "he expected and encouraged me to deal with the difficult Hebrew text philologically… let the stories themselves give theological teachings and devotional insights."
- **Locus:** Preface / raw ~L189–191
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-2-samuel-nicot]]

### C-R0-02 | Intended audience: early Divided Monarchy (late 10th c.), not Persian era
- **Claim:** Meaning sought is that intended for early Divided Monarchy readers (late tenth century B.C. or a little later), not Persian-era sixth-century readers as often advocated.
- **Quote:** "readers of the early Divided Monarchy, possibly of the late tenth century B.C. or a little later, not readers of the Persian era of the sixth century B.C."
- **Locus:** Preface / raw ~L193
- **Targets:** [[2-samuel]], [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R0-03 | Defends 1 Samuel method against critics
- **Claim:** Grateful for critical attention to 1 Samuel volume; remains convinced of approach: many MT texts supportable vs LXX as *lectio difficilior*; linguistic solutions rather than changing text (since 1998); does not use consensus Deuteronomistic redaction; synchronic reading has priority over diachronic; diachronic ≠ historical/spatio-temporal; responds to “lack of literary treatment” criticism — text must be fixed first before literary analysis; hopes literary critics will use the commentary for dialogical/intertextual work on a solid Hebrew text; points to Intro on intertextuality and wise woman of Tekoa (2 Sam 14).
- **Quote:** "I still believe that many, if not all, MT texts can be supported as against the LXX as lectio difficilior… a synchronic reading should have a priority over a diachronic one"
- **Locus:** Preface / raw ~L195
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]], [[tsumura-1-samuel-nicot]], [[2-samuel]]

### C-R0-04 | Project history; Gordon encouragement; Tsukuba linguistics
- **Claim:** Project began 1990; shift from ANE/linguistics to OT teaching at Japan Bible Seminary; preferred poetic books (Habakkuk → Psalms/Job) but accepted Samuel at Gordon’s encouragement; Ugaritic/Canaanite and Tsukuba linguistics prepared him for Samuel’s textual problems; 1 Samuel completed 2007.
- **Quote:** "my training in Canaanite religion and culture as well as in Semitic philology, especially Ugaritic, might contribute to clarifying some difficult exegetical problems."
- **Locus:** Preface / raw ~L197
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]]

### C-R0-05 | Acknowledgments; dedication Prov 3:6
- **Claim:** Thanks A. R. Millard, R. L. Hubbard (two decades’ patience), A. Knapp (editorial); wife Susan (MIT-trained linguist) as companion; dedicated to her with Prov 3:6 Hebrew.
- **Quote:** "To her, I dedicate this book with love and thanks."
- **Locus:** Preface / raw ~L199–201
- **Targets:** [[david-tsumura]]

Preface only; footnotes in range acknowledge Habakkuk articles, Polak evaluation of vol. 1 discourse grammar, Dietrich reception volumes — apparatus-level.
